descriptionChirho: A seasonal watercourse or brook, typically dry in summer and flowing in the rainy season; the default sense of nachal used for named wadis (Kidron, Arnon, Besor, Eshcol, etc.) and for generic brooks in pastoral and narrative contexts — Arabic وَادِي (wadi), Korean 시내 (brook/stream), Swahili kijito (brook) or bonde (valley-wadi), Spanish arroyo.

A geographic depression or narrow valley carved by seasonal water flow, emphasizing the landform rather than the watercourse; target languages consistently shift to valley-specific terms — Arabic وَادٍ/الْوَادِي (valley), Korean 골짜기/계곡 (valley/gorge), Swahili bonde (valley), Spanish valle.

A permanent flowing watercourse, larger and more sustained than a seasonal brook; used for rivers of Egypt, Mesopotamia, and in poetic/wisdom contexts for streams of abundance — Arabic نَهْر (river), Korean 강 (river), Swahili mto (river), Spanish río; distinct from the seasonal wadi sense.

The rushing, often destructive surge of water through a wadi during flash floods; used in similes and poetic descriptions of overwhelming force — Arabic سَيْل (torrent/flood), Korean 급류 (torrent), Swahili mkondo (current), Spanish torrente; emphasizes the dynamic, dangerous water flow rather than the channel.
